reference.title: Dumbbell Rear Fly
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Shoulders, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you raise the arms, breathe in as you lower; keep the trunk braced.
breathing.cadence: About 1.5 s up, short squeeze, about 2 s down

prescription.load: User-chosen dumbbells; light, so the back stays flat
prescription.progression: Add reps, then weight; chest-supported rear fly on an incline bench

cues.text: Feet hip width, knees soft, hinge at the hips until the trunk is nearly parallel to the floor with a flat back. Dumbbells hang under the shoulders, palms facing each other.
Breathe out and sweep the arms out to the sides with soft elbows, leading with the backs of the hands.
Arms about level with the back; squeeze the shoulder blades together briefly.
Lower slowly back under the shoulders; keep the trunk still.
Stay in the hinge, reset and repeat.

mistakes.fix: Push the hips back, keep the chest long; stand a little more upright if needed.

mistakes.mistake: Rowing (bending the elbows a lot and pulling back)
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbow bend fixed and move the arms out to the sides.

mistakes.mistake: Jerking the trunk up to swing the weights
mistakes.fix: Keep the trunk still; use lighter dumbbells.
Draw the shoulder blades back and down.

kinematics.norm: Nearly parallel to the floor, flat back (clinical opinion)
From arms hanging to about level with the back; prone horizontal abduction tested at about 100 degrees of abduction (Reinold 2007)
Neutral (palms facing each other) gave more posterior deltoid and infraspinatus activity than pronated (Schoenfeld 2013)

sources.title: GymVisual #037812, Dumbbell Rear Fly, video (movement reference)
Schoenfeld et al. 2013, effect of hand position on EMG activity of the posterior shoulder musculature during a horizontal abduction exercise (J Strength Cond Res 27(10):2644-2649)
Reinold et al. 2007, electromyographic analysis of the supraspinatus and deltoid muscles during 3 common rehabilitation exercises (J Athl Train 42(4):464-469)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with good form.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
The bent-over position loads the low back; keep the back flat and the weights light.
modify: Low-back discomfort: do it chest-supported, lying face down on an incline bench, or seated bent over the end of a bench.
Hamstring tightness: bend the knees more.
regressions: Chest-supported rear delt fly on an incline bench.
progressions: Slower 3 s lowering with a 1 s squeeze.

muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Prime mover (horizontal abduction). A neutral grip gave more posterior deltoid activity than a pronated grip on a reverse fly (Schoenfeld 2013); prone horizontal abduction reached about 87% MVIC in the posterior deltoid (Reinold 2007).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Prime mover (horizontal abduction). A neutral grip gave more posterior deltoid activity than a pronated grip on a reverse fly (Schoenfeld 2013); prone horizontal abduction reached about 87% MVIC in the posterior deltoid (Reinold 2007).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: External rotator that works with the posterior deltoid; higher with a neutral grip (Schoenfeld 2013).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: External rotator that works with the posterior deltoid; higher with a neutral grip (Schoenfeld 2013).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Helps lift the arm; prone horizontal abduction also gave about 63% MVIC in the middle deltoid (Reinold 2007).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Helps lift the arm; prone horizontal abduction also gave about 63% MVIC in the middle deltoid (Reinold 2007).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the flat back in the hip hinge for the whole set.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the flat back in the hip hinge for the whole set.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Hold the hinge at the hips with the knees soft.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Hold the hinge at the hips with the knees soft.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Holds the hips in the hinge.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Holds the hips in the hinge.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk still so the arms do the work.

guides.label: Arms sweep out to the sides
